abstract: Abstract Background While Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCE) have been used extensively in medical education, a virtual OSCE has yet to be implemented. Methods This cross-sectional pilot validation study included all 12 clinical medical students participating in the emergency medicine clinical rotation from October to November 2022. abstract: Abstract Background Conventional single best answer tests (SBATs) are a proven and ubiquitous assessment tool. By their very nature, SBATs prompt students to guess a correct outcome when unsure of the answer, which may lead to a reduced ability to reliably assay student knowledge. Confidence-based answer tests (CBATs) are designed to improve reliability because participants are not forced to guess where they cannot choose between two or more alternative answers which they may favour equally. Educators aim to develop assessments for learning rather than assessment of learning; although both SBATs and CBATS have proven benefits, as CBATs provide additional information about student confidence, they may provide additional insights to educators and students alike. However, their use may be limited if they significantly alter student scores or grades compared to SBATs. The aim of this study was to compare performance across these test paradigms, to investigate if there are any systematic biases present and to analyse student perceptions qualitatively. In clinical pharmacy, assessing medication-related care competencies remains challenging due to a lack of standardized frameworks adaptable to digital learning environments. This scoping review mapped competency assessment methods across healthcare disciplines, evaluated reported validation approaches, and identified tools adaptable to clinical pharmacy education and independent, asynchronous e-learning. abstract: Abstract Background The integration of traditional and modern educational approaches in contemporary curricula, particularly in medical education, is becoming increasingly necessary. Medical schools and healthcare institutions are seeking to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of training programs, while medical educators grapple with challenges such as the rapid expansion of medical knowledge, the need for lifelong learning, evolving learner expectations, and technological advancements in clinical education. Microlearning, a learner-centered approach that delivers content in small, digestible chunks, has emerged as a promising solution. Recent studies suggest that incorporating microlearning into traditional teaching methods may help address some of these challenges effectively. Task-based learning, another student-centered approach, emphasizes practical skill development through problem-solving and task completion. abstract: Abstract Background Whether perceived technical AI competency is associated with greater ethical openness to AI integration, a relationship often assumed in curricular design, remains empirically untested. This pilot study examined relationships between perceived AI readiness, ethical perspectives toward AI integration, and curricular needs among medical students. Methods A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical students at a single U.S. institution from September through November 2025. abstract: Abstract Background Advances in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology, expanding clinical applications, and reduced scan times have led to increased demand for MRI services. abstract: Abstract Background Beyond technical feasibility of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated multiple-choice questions (MCQs), their educational value in assessment remains unclear. Methods In this cross-sectional study 119 year five medical students completed a Family Medicine MCQ tablet-based exam. Participants answered 30 AI-generated and 30 NLE MCQs. AI questions were generated from digital learning materials using ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro. abstract: Abstract Background Emergency Medicine (EM) is a critical specialty focused on the rapid assessment and management of life-threatening conditions. EM faces significant challenges in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where 90% of healthcare emergencies occur. This study assessed medical students’ clinical knowledge of common medical emergencies, attitudes toward EM as a specialty, and perceptions and factors influencing consideration of EM as a career. abstract: Abstract Background More than one billion people worldwide, and more than one in four US adults, have a disability, yet continue to face barriers to equitable healthcare. Evidence links these disparities to inadequate professional preparation: limited disability-focused content, persistent ableist attitudes, and the absence of structured competency frameworks. This scoping review mapped how current disability competency frameworks guide curriculum development in healthcare education, identifying frameworks, instructional approaches, and outcomes across disciplines and contexts. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Databases searched, in collaboration with a health sciences librarian, included Medline, CINAHL, Embase, and Scopus. Studies were eligible if they were peer-reviewed, published from 2010 onward, available in English, and used an identifiable framework, competency set, model, theory, or professional standard to guide disability-focused education within a formal healthcare education program. abstract: Abstract Background On-call simulation has been used as an effective means to address feelings of under-preparedness amongst new doctors transitioning into clinical practice. Traditional “bleep” simulations are delivered in-situ, in the clinical environment using dedicated pager devices. However, these simulations are often limited by a high facilitator burden and resistance from perceived disruption of clinical environments. Tabletop alternatives to in-situ modalities offer solutions to scalability issues, particularly in the context of large cohorts requiring training. abstract: Abstract Background The prevalence of stress and stress injury among healthcare professionals and students is well-documented and exacerbated by long work hours, high patient volume, and challenging working conditions. Traditional well-being programs have focused on individual resilience, often neglecting the importance of peer support and a culture of caring. The Stress First Aid for Healthcare Workers (SFA-HCW) program, originally developed by the Department of Defense, was adapted for health professions students, staff, and faculty at Duke University and North Carolina Central University (NCCU). This program aims to improve confidence in delivering peer support and promote long-term well-being. The SFA-HCW program addresses stress in a “pre-clinical” phase, making it accessible to lay audiences. It equips participants to recognize and respond to stress injuries in peers while preserving life, preventing further harm, and promoting recovery. title: What makes remediation matter? A qualitative study of medical students’ experiences of a pilot online remediation programme in Chemical Pathology
abstract: Abstract Background Remediation supports underperforming students whilst protecting academic standards and patient safety. We piloted a formal online remedial programme for underperforming second-year medical students in Chemical Pathology within the Semester 4 Integrated Health Systems curriculum at the University of Cape Town. This paper reports the qualitative findings and uses Vygotskian scaffolding to interpret students’ accounts of the programme’s educational value and design limitations. Methods This qualitative study was nested within a broader pilot evaluation of a short, time-bound online programme delivered via a learning management system. Ten of the twelve eligible students who completed the mandatory remediation programme and qualified for the supplementary examination participated in a post-intervention focus group discussion conducted face-to-face. The discussion was audio-recorded, transcribed and analysed inductively using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. abstract: Abstract Background Health disparities remain a persistent challenge in medicine, exacerbated by inequitable practices within healthcare systems and among professionals. abstract: Abstract Germany faces critical physician shortages in Neurology. This exploratory study examined factors influencing career decision-making across the Neurology training pipeline in a university setting to inform workforce development strategies. We conducted a cross-sectional two cohort study employing a mixed-methods approach surveying medical students (n = 79) and Neurology residents (n = 56) at German University hospitals via structured questionnaires and open-ended questions. The response rates were 44 % (medical students) and 32 % (residents). The important factors influencing career and medical specialization choices were the specialty itself, good teaching experiences and workplace conditions. Students showed high career motivation. Residents maintained high levels of engagement and specialty loyalty while reporting severe structural deficits in their everyday worklife and residency program. abstract: Abstract Sport-related injuries remain a significant challenge in sports medicine. Dental trauma, particularly permanent tooth avulsion, remains an underrecognized injury in physically active populations. The study aimed to assess medical students’ awareness, theoretical knowledge, and practical skills regarding the prevention and emergency management of permanent tooth avulsion, with particular emphasis on the potential application of these competencies in sport-related settings. Materials and methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 291 medical students. A validated questionnaire was used to assess their understanding of primary prevention, theoretical knowledge, and practical skills. abstract: Abstract Background Gamification has emerged as an innovative teaching methodology, particularly in nursing education, fostering engagement and active learning. Objective To translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Gameful Experience Scale (GAMEX) for Brazilian Portuguese. Methods A methodological, quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted in three phases: linguistic and cultural adaptation, content validation, and construct validation. abstract: Abstract Background Sense of belonging (SoB) may support participation and engagement in online distance learning (ODL), yet little is known about how postgraduate health professions learners understand and experience it. Methods A qualitative multi-site case study was conducted across four medical universities in Pakistan, each offering postgraduate health professions education programmes and treated as a distinct case to capture both shared and institution-specific patterns.
